title: Explain Dropout at Inference
prompt:
A model was trained with dropout. What should change at inference time, and why?

Explain the difference between inverted dropout and test-time scaling, and describe how you would ensure the model is in the correct mode.

response.placeholder: State the dropout convention before describing the inference-time computation.
response.reference_answer:
## Standard behavior

During training, dropout randomly zeroes activations. In the common inverted-dropout convention, each retained activation is scaled by 1 / (1 - p), where p is the drop probability. That keeps the training-time activation expectation aligned with the full network. At ordinary inference, disable dropout and use the full network; under this convention the evaluation-time dropout layer is the identity.

## Convention and operational checks

Older formulations instead leave retained activations unscaled during training and apply the corresponding scale at test time. Both conventions can represent the same intended expectation, but an answer should say which one it assumes rather than combining them.

Switch the model to evaluation mode so dropout is disabled and train/eval-sensitive modules such as BatchNorm use evaluation behavior. Evaluation mode alone does not necessarily disable autograd; inference code should also avoid building gradients when they are not needed. Deliberately retaining dropout for Monte Carlo uncertainty estimates is a special inference technique, not the standard prediction path.
